body:
## What to build

Retain lexical ownership of `.BY` established through string assignment targets or indirect assignment calls when a dtplyr Margin summary also contains contextual shares. If a form cannot be supported safely, refuse it rather than returning a different aggregate.

## Evidence and reproduction

Investigated on main snapshot `4c63bb917ed7ed31ff6aadf060a5eae7a32cd004` with R 4.6.1, data.table 1.18.6.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, and dplyr 1.2.1. This ticket records a confirmed bug-hunt finding; no repair was implemented during the investigation.

Use g equal to a,b, an otherwise unused input `.BY` column equal to 1,3, and x equal to 2,6. Summarize sum(x) as value and an independent expression that locally binds the name `.BY` to 5,7 and sums that binding. Add a share of value over a rollup of g. Writing the assignment target as the string `.BY` makes the independent output become 1,3,4 instead of the lexical result 12,12,12. Renaming only the unused input column makes the lazy control return 12,12,12. The local control also returns that result; ordinary dtplyr and the no-share path refuse these forms rather than silently changing their values.

Six forms reproduced across both helpers and direct/across share-source styles: string targets with left and right assignment, a string-target assignment in a function body, assignment through do.call, and computed assign callees resolved through get or match.fun. These were 24 silently wrong results. Generated queries showed the lexical read replaced by the input-column alias, while the assignment retained its original target.

#1033 fixed formal-bound and directly recognized local assignments. Its repair still misses these assignment spellings. This follow-up concerns that incomplete binding analysis; explicit evaluation masks are a separate finding. All caller tables remained unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six forms either retain the lexical result or receive an appropriate refusal. They never successfully return values from the unrelated input `.BY` column.
- [ ] Binding analysis accounts for string assignment targets and conservatively handles unresolved assignment callees, including function-body scope.
- [ ] Public regressions cover both helpers and preserve successful safe-input-name controls plus the existing formal/direct-assignment behavior.
- [ ] Preserve direct/across input-measure `.BY` support, source validation, lazy construction, and caller-table isolation.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[PR #1052](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1052) records the dated audit, executable reproductions, successful controls, expected failing repair assertions, and version/scope limits.
title: [P2] Preserve string and indirect .BY bindings in dtplyr share lowering
